story: When the gods had to work like humans, the lower gods (the Igigu) dug canals and rivers to sustain the land, while the upper gods (the Anunnaki) ruled over them. After 40 years the lower gods rebelled, surrounding the dwelling of Enlil, chief of the gods. Enlil consulted Anu and Enki; his messenger Nusku failed to negotiate peace. To avoid battle, Enlil proposed creating humans to do the gods' hard labor. He asked Mami, leader of seven divine wombs, to help; she required Enki's aid. The gods purified themselves, then Enki slaughtered a lesser god, Geshtu-E, mixing his blood with clay to form the first human. Mami gave the creature a basket and taught it to labor. A woman was placed beside the man, and at Mami's command they reproduced. Mami had them celebrate a seven-day feast for Ishtar, and after nine months the first child was born. After 1200 years, humans multiplied and grew noisy, so Enlil sent Namtar to kill many with plague. Enki told his priest Atrahasis to have people worship only Namtar, who grew ashamed and stopped. After another 1200 years, humans multiplied again; Enlil sent Adad, then Nisaba, to bring storms and famine. Enki again advised Atrahasis to redirect worship, shaming these gods into stopping. Enraged, Enlil decreed a flood to destroy humanity and forced Enki to swear silence. Enki secretly instructed Atrahasis, speaking to a reed wall, to build a cube-shaped, waterproof ship, gather food and animals, and prepare for seven days of flood. Atrahasis built the ship with neighbors' help, promising future rewards, then he and his family and a fertile couple boarded and sealed the ship as storms began.
